Subject: Guarantee band & repricing — HeliosHealth order form

Hi Grace / Karthik,

Thanks for sending the draft exhibit. Procurement has one substantive open area before we can route for signature: the "guarantee band" and repricing mechanics tied to the order form. Two quick asks so we can close this week: 1) Confirm how the guarantee band is defined (is it a percentage collar around committed units or an absolute band by $?), and 2) confirm the annual repricing / true-up calculation and whether there are caps/floors on movement.

Specifically, our audit team wants clarity on whether repricing can move both up and down and how credits/charges are applied for variance vs commit. If you can provide redline language or a short summary of the proposed economic guardrails, procurement will evaluate immediately.

We attached the exhibit we received — please mark up and return. We're targeting signature by end of next week, so expedited review would be appreciated.

Thanks,
Evan
Evan Diaz
Director, Cloud Ops
Helios Health

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Guarantee band & repricing — HeliosHealth order form
Attachments: GRD_redline_exhibit_v3.docx (attachment)

Evan — thanks for the clear asks. High level: we want a mechanism that balances predictability for you with price stability for long‑tail usage. Our suggested compromise (detailed in the attached redline) is as follows: 

- Guarantee band: defined as a +/- 20% collar around the committed monthly token units (expressed in billed units). The band is applied to the annualized commit for true‑up calculation.
- Annual repricing / true‑up: an annual true‑up reconciles actual billed units vs committed annual units. Repricing is two‑way but smoothed: per‑year movement is capped at +/- 7.5% to avoid sharp step changes. Cumulative movement over the first three years is capped at +/- 25%.
- Credits/charges: variance inside the band is billed at the standard rate. Variance outside the band triggers a true‑up invoice or credit, calculated on a pro‑rata basis for the period in which variance occurred. We propose an optional one‑time reconciliation credit if year‑1 usage exceeds the band by >50% (to protect short ramp scenarios).
- Audit & governance: Redwood retains the right to audit usage once per year with 30 days' notice; any underreporting found will be reconciled with interest at the contractual rate.

Neha, I've looped you to confirm the redline language — the goal is to keep the economics concrete (percent collars, caps) rather than open‑ended floors. Evan, if that structure is acceptable in principle we'll prepare an amended exhibit for signature and include a short SOW note on how overage invoice cadence works.

Next steps: if you agree in principle, I'll send a DocuSign packet with the amended exhibit and schedule a 30‑minute call early next week to walk procurement through the math.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 09:12:03 -07:00
Subject: Re: Guarantee band & repricing — HeliosHealth order form

Grace / Karthik — reviewed the proposed economic guardrails. I made a few changes in the attached redline that we should push back or clarify with Helios before finalizing: 

1) Replace the term "floor" with "minimum annual commitment" and explicitly tie any minimum to the signed order form amount. Avoids ambiguity about whether a pricing "floor" allows unilateral downward repricing.
2) Repricing mechanics: keep the smoothing band (+/- 7.5% annual cap) but add an explicit non‑retroactivity clause: any repricing applies only to invoices issued after the new effective date and does not reprice invoices already paid.
3) Reconciliation timing & dispute: require that disputed true‑up invoices be raised within 45 days of issuance and include an expedited dispute process (15 business days review, then escrow of undisputed amount).
4) Audit scope: narrow audit to usage logs and billing records and limit to one in any 12‑month period unless material discrepancies (>5%) are found.
5) Termination trigger: clarify that a persistent negative variance (usage < 60% of commit for two consecutive quarters) permits Redwood to renegotiate pricing or suspend credits after a cure period.

Below is a suggested clause snippet you can include in the exhibit redline (drop‑in language):

"Guarantee Band and Repricing. The parties agree that the Customer's annual committed units shall be subject to a guarantee band defined as +/- 20% of the committed amount ("Guarantee Band"). An annual true‑up shall reconcile actual billed units against the committed units. Adjustments resulting from the true‑up shall be effective prospectively and limited to +/- 7.5% per contract year (the "Annual Adjustment Cap"), with cumulative adjustments capped at +/- 25% over any three‑year rolling period. Any reconciliation amount not disputed in writing within forty‑five (45) days of invoice issuance shall be payable in accordance with the invoice terms. Audit rights are limited to usage and billing records once per twelve (12) month period unless materially inconsistent results (>5%) are identified."

I think the combination of numeric collars, non‑retroactivity, and a narrow audit scope will clear procurement's concerns while protecting Redwood's commercial position. Happy to join a call with Evan if needed.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Evan — thanks for the quick turnaround. We've incorporated Neha's counsel and attached a final exhibit PDF for your review. Key points of the final exhibit (short):

- Guarantee band: +/- 20% collar around the annualized commit.
- Annual true‑up with +/- 7.5% per year smoothing; cumulative 25% cap over three years.
- Non‑retroactivity and 45‑day dispute window; limited audit scope.
- One‑time ramp credit (applies if year‑1 usage > 50% above commit) to address short ramp risk.

If that aligns with procurement's expectations, we've published the amended exhibit to DocuSign here: https://www.docusign.com/helios/exhibit-amendment-7832

Thanks — we want to keep the deal moving for your Q2 launch.
